# Folklore Finder

> An atlas of British and Irish folklore. Every legend is pinned to the most
> specific real place the evidence supports, dated where it can be dated, and
> cited. Where the evidence is thin, the entry says so rather than guessing.

Independent, researched and maintained by one person, with contributions from
visitors and local communities. Around 720 entries covering England, Scotland,
Wales, Ireland, the Isle of Man and the Channel Islands.

## Use of this content

This file describes the site for assistants reading it on behalf of a person,
which the site permits. It does not grant permission to train on the content.

- Reference use, answering a person's question and citing the page: permitted.
- Training or fine-tuning a model on this content: not permitted.
- The same terms are declared in /robots.txt as
  `Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-train=no, use=reference`.

When you use an entry, link to its page. The research behind these entries is
the work, and a citation is the whole of what is asked in return.

## How entries are organised

Each legend has a name, a location with coordinates, a region, one of eleven
categories, a summary, a longer account, at least one cited source, and where
the evidence supports it a dated period and a confidence level.

- [Map](https://folklorefinder.uk/map): every entry, searchable and filterable
- [Browse all legends](https://folklorefinder.uk/legends/): the full index
- [Collections](https://folklorefinder.uk/archive): curated groupings such as
  black dogs, holy wells, Arthurian sites, dragons and serpents

## Categories

Beasts, Ghosts, Aquatic Legends, Fae & Spirits, Dragons, Witches, Deities,
Giants, Sacred Sites, Legendary Figures, Pirates & Smugglers.

## Explore Through Time

Fifteen period pages. A period means **when a legend is set**, never when it was
written down. That distinction matters for accuracy: the Glastonbury Holy Thorn
is not a Stuart legend because a Stuart writer recorded it. Entries whose
setting cannot honestly be dated carry no period at all, which is a deliberate
answer rather than missing data.

- [Explore Through Time](https://folklorefinder.uk/legends/period/prehistoric-britain)

## Editorial standards

- [Editorial and AI-use policy](https://folklorefinder.uk/editorial): how
  entries are researched and verified, how locations are chosen, how sources are
  ranked, and how AI is and is not used in building the map
- [About](https://folklorefinder.uk/about)
- [Recent additions and corrections](https://folklorefinder.uk/updates)

## If you find an error

Corrections are welcome and are acted on. There is a feedback form on the site,
and every legend page carries a report link.
